[1;38;5;208mSHELLTUTOR[0m  —  a vimtutor prerequisite course

Welcome. A short hands-on course in [1;38;5;244mfive stages[0m that
prepare you for [1;38;5;220mvimtutor[0m. About 45 to 60 minutes total.

Each stage is a few short lessons followed by a small task. Pass the
task to advance. Retry as much as you like — no time pressure, no
skip.

Your work happens in [38;5;109m/var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-vlcywnbb[0m; the tutor never writes
outside that folder.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m for a quick orientation.[0m

[1;38;5;208mOrientation[0m

In a moment you'll be at the practice prompt below. It looks like:

    [2mshelltutor>[0m

Type a command, press Enter — the shell runs it. The terminal is
keyboard-only; you can't click mid-line to move the cursor. Resize
your terminal larger if text wraps (80×24 or bigger).

[1;38;5;244mFour words steer the tutor:[0m
  [1;38;5;220mnext[0m  advance        [1;38;5;220mprev[0m  go back
  [1;38;5;220mshow[0m  redisplay      [1;38;5;220mquit[0m  leave (progress saved)

A fifth word, [1;38;5;220mcheck[0m, appears at gate tasks when relevant.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to begin Stage 1.[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 1 — Where am I?[0m

Four short lessons (about 10 minutes) followed by a small task.
You'll meet the prompt, run a few simple commands, and learn the
keyboard habits that make the shell easy to live with.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to start lesson 1.1.[0m

[1;38;5;208m1.1 — running commands[0m

At the prompt below, type this and press Enter:

  [1;38;5;220mecho hello[0m

You'll see [2mhello[0m printed, then the prompt comes back. Now try:

  [1;38;5;220mecho I am at the shell[0m      [2m# spaces separate words[0m
  [1;38;5;220mecho "I am at the shell"[0m    [2m# quotes group them into one[0m

[1;38;5;220mecho[0m just repeats its words back. It is the simplest command
there is, and its shape is the shape of every command you'll meet:
a name, then the words you hand it.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Try all three, then type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m.[0m
echo I am at the shell

echo I am at the shell
[?2004l

[1;38;5;208m1.2 — keyboard habits[0m

Four keys make the shell comfortable. Try each one now.

  [38;5;208mTab[0m       bash finishes a word. Type [1;38;5;220mecho p[0m, press [38;5;208mTab[0m:
            it becomes [1;38;5;220mecho poem.txt[0m. Several matches? The first
            [38;5;208mTab[0m fills in the shared part; [38;5;208mTab[0m again lists them.
            (Other shells and setups differ.)
  [38;5;208m↑[0m         brings back the last command. Enter runs it again.
  [38;5;208mCtrl+L[0m    clears the screen; the command [1;38;5;220mclear[0m does the same.
            Type [1;38;5;220mshow[0m to bring this lesson back afterwards.
  [38;5;208mCtrl+C[0m    the escape hatch. If anything feels stuck, press it
            and you get a fresh prompt.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Try each key, then type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m.[0m

[1;38;5;208m1.3 — where am I, who am I, when is it[0m

Three commands that ask the system about itself.

  [1;38;5;220mwhoami[0m     [2m# the user name you're logged in as[0m
  [1;38;5;220mpwd[0m        [2m# print working directory — the folder you're in[0m
  [1;38;5;220mdate[0m       [2m# the current date and time[0m

Here [1;38;5;220mpwd[0m shows the tutor's own folder, because that is where
this practice prompt starts. Stage 2 is all about folders.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Run all three, then type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m.[0m

[1;38;5;208m1.4 — what just happened[0m

When you type [1;38;5;220mwhoami[0m and press Enter:

  1. The terminal hands your line to [1;38;5;244mthe shell[0m.
  2. The shell looks for a program named [1;38;5;220mwhoami[0m.
  3. It runs it.
  4. The program prints to [1;38;5;244mstandard output[0m — your screen.
  5. The shell shows the prompt again, ready for the next command.

The shell is not "Unix." It is a program — a [1;38;5;244mcommand interpreter[0m.
The terminal is a window that lets you talk to the shell. The program
[1;38;5;220mwhoami[0m is a third thing — it runs, prints, and exits.

You will keep these three apart for the rest of this tutor:
  [1;38;5;244mterminal[0m  →  [1;38;5;244mshell[0m  →  [1;38;5;244mprogram[0m

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to take Stage 1's gate.[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 1 — GATE[0m

[1;38;5;244mRecall[0m (three questions, all three must be correct).

Then a [1;38;5;244mpractical task[0m: run a few commands and tell me what
they printed. The script verifies your answers.

[2mUnlimited retries. No skip.[0m
[1;38;5;39mQ1: Which character usually ends a shell prompt? ($, ;, :, or #)[0m

[1;38;5;39mQ3: After [1;38;5;220mwhoami[0m runs, where does its output go?[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 1 — GATE TASK[0m

Inside the practice prompt, run each of these once. Read each output.
Then type [1;38;5;220mcheck[0m.

  [1;38;5;220mwhoami[0m
  [1;38;5;220mpwd[0m
  [1;38;5;220mdate[0m

After all three have run, I'll ask you what each one printed.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mcheck[1;38;5;208m only after running all three.[0m

[1;38;5;244mThree short follow-ups based on what you saw.[0m

[1;38;5;39mWhat did [1;38;5;220mwhoami[1;38;5;39m print? (just the username)[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;39mWhat did [1;38;5;220mpwd[1;38;5;39m print? (paste the full path)[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;39mWhat day of the week did [1;38;5;220mdate[1;38;5;39m show? (Mon, Tue, … — or exactly as date printed it)[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 2 — Paths and the filesystem[0m

Three lessons, then a gate. The shell is always [1;38;5;244msomewhere[0m in
the filesystem; this stage teaches you to move around and to predict
where files land.

You'll use:
  [1;38;5;220mls[0m    list what's in the current folder
  [1;38;5;220mcd[0m    change to another folder
  [1;38;5;220mpwd[0m   print where you are now

And the path symbols:
  [1;38;5;244m.[0m     this folder
  [1;38;5;244m..[0m    the parent folder
  [1;38;5;244m~[0m     your home folder

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to begin lesson 2.1.[0m

[1;38;5;208m2.1 — ls: what's in here[0m

[1;38;5;220mls[0m lists files and folders in your current directory.

  [1;38;5;220mls[0m            [2m# names only[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls -l[0m         [2m# long form (permissions, size, date)[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls -a[0m         [2m# include hidden files (those starting with .)[0m

Try each. Then [1;38;5;220mls[0m a folder you don't [1;38;5;220mcd[0m into:
  [1;38;5;220mls /etc[0m       [2m# system config folder[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls /usr/bin[0m   [2m# where many commands live[0m

([2m/etc[0m and [2m/usr/bin[0m exist on both Linux and macOS.)

[1;38;5;208m2.2 — cd and the home folder[0m

[1;38;5;220mcd[0m changes your current folder.

  [1;38;5;220mcd /tmp[0m       [2m# go to /tmp[0m
  [1;38;5;220mpwd[0m           [2m# confirm you got there[0m
  [1;38;5;220mcd[0m            [2m# go home (just 'cd' by itself)[0m
  [1;38;5;220mcd ~[0m          [2m# also go home — ~ means $HOME[0m

Two more useful ones:
  [1;38;5;220mcd -[0m          [2m# go back to the previous folder[0m
  [1;38;5;220mcd ..[0m         [2m# go up one level (to the parent folder)[0m

[1;38;5;196mStages 1 and 2 start every practice prompt in[0m [38;5;109m/var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-vlcywnbb[0m[1;38;5;196m.[0m
Later stages start in a stage folder inside it. If you wander off,
[1;38;5;220mcd /var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-vlcywnbb[0m brings you back.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to continue.[0m

[1;38;5;208m2.3 — paths: relative, absolute, dot, dot-dot[0m

A [1;38;5;244mpath[0m tells the shell where something is.

[1;38;5;244mRelative paths[0m start where you are now:
  [2mnotes.txt[0m            a file in this folder
  [2mpractice/notes.txt[0m   a file inside a subfolder
  [2m../notes.txt[0m         a file in the parent folder
  [2m./notes.txt[0m          same as 'notes.txt' (the . is this folder)

[1;38;5;244mAbsolute paths[0m start from the root, with [38;5;208m/[0m:
  [2m/etc/hosts[0m
  [2m/usr/bin/vim[0m
  [2m/home/alice/notes.txt[0m

[1;38;5;244m~[0m is short for your home folder. [2m~/notes[0m means
[2m$HOME/notes[0m.

[1;38;5;196mPredict before you act.[0m  If you're in [2m~/projects[0m
and you type [1;38;5;220mcat notes.txt[0m, the shell looks for
[2m~/projects/notes.txt[0m. If you mean a different folder, name it.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to take Stage 2's gate.[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 2 — GATE[0m

[1;38;5;244mRecall[0m (three questions, all three must be correct).
Then a [1;38;5;244mpractical task[0m.
[1;38;5;39mQ2: What does [1;38;5;220m~[0m mean in a path?[0m

[1;38;5;39mQ3: If I'm in [2m~/projects[0m and I type [1;38;5;220mcd notes[0m, what folder am I in?[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 2 — GATE TASK[0m

Inside the practice prompt, do these (in any order):

  1. make a folder called [38;5;109mpractice[0m (inside this stage's folder)
  2. cd into it
  3. confirm you're inside it with [1;38;5;220mpwd[0m

Then type [1;38;5;220mcheck[0m. I'll look for [38;5;109mpractice[0m on disk.

[2mHint: [1;38;5;220mmkdir practice[0m[2m creates the folder.[0m

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mcheck[1;38;5;208m when done.[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 3 — Files and operations[0m

Three lessons, then a gate. You'll create, read, copy, move, and remove
files. [1;38;5;196mrm is immediate.[0m It does not move things to a trash.
We'll do everything inside [38;5;109m/var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-vlcywnbb/stage3[0m so practice is
contained.

Commands this stage:
  [1;38;5;220mtouch[0m   create an empty file (or update its timestamp)
  [1;38;5;220mmkdir[0m   create a folder
  [1;38;5;220mrmdir[0m   remove an EMPTY folder
  [1;38;5;220mcat[0m     print a text file
  [1;38;5;220mless[0m    page through a long file (exit with [38;5;208mq[0m)
  [1;38;5;220mcp[0m      copy
  [1;38;5;220mmv[0m      move (or rename — same command)
  [1;38;5;220mrm[0m      remove a file ([1;38;5;196mimmediate[0m)

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to begin lesson 3.1.[0m

[1;38;5;208m3.1 — creating: touch, mkdir[0m

[1;38;5;220mtouch[0m creates an empty file (or updates the timestamp of
an existing one).
  [1;38;5;220mtouch hello.txt[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls[0m              [2m# you should see hello.txt[0m

[1;38;5;220mmkdir[0m creates a folder.
  [1;38;5;220mmkdir notes[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls[0m              [2m# notes/ is now there[0m

To create a file [1;38;5;244mwith content[0m, use redirection (Stage 4):
  [1;38;5;220mecho "first line" > greeting.txt[0m

But for now, [1;38;5;220mtouch[0m for empty files, [1;38;5;220mmkdir[0m for
folders.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Make a few, then [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m.[0m

[1;38;5;208m3.2 — reading: cat, less[0m

[1;38;5;220mcat[0m prints the entire file at once.
  [1;38;5;220mcat hello.txt[0m                [2m# probably empty[0m
  [1;38;5;220mcat ../poem.txt[0m        [2m# the tutor's poem, one folder up[0m

For a long file, [1;38;5;220mcat[0m floods the screen. Use [1;38;5;220mless[0m
to page through it:
  [1;38;5;220mless ../numbers.txt[0m    [2m# 50 lines — more than one screen[0m

Inside [1;38;5;220mless[0m, the screen takes over. Press [38;5;208mSpace[0m
or [38;5;208mf[0m to page down, [38;5;208mb[0m to page back, and
[38;5;208mq[0m to exit. (More on full-screen programs in Stage 5.)

[1;38;5;196mImportant:[0m when [1;38;5;220mless[0m takes over, the prompt is
gone. You're inside a program. [38;5;208mq[0m returns you to the shell.

[1;38;5;208m▶ Try both, then [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m.[0m

The terminal is a quiet room.
You speak to it, it answers back.
Words have shapes here, and shapes have weight.
A pipe is a doorway between rooms.

[1;38;5;208m3.3 — copy, move, delete[0m

[1;38;5;220mcp[0m copies. The original stays.
  [1;38;5;220mcp hello.txt backup.txt[0m

[1;38;5;220mmv[0m moves. The original moves to the new name or folder.
The same command is used for [1;38;5;244mrename[0m:
  [1;38;5;220mmv hello.txt hi.txt[0m            [2m# rename[0m
  [1;38;5;220mmv hi.txt notes/[0m               [2m# move into a folder[0m

[1;38;5;220mrm[0m deletes. [1;38;5;196mImmediately and permanently.[0m
  [1;38;5;220mrm backup.txt[0m

There is no Trash to recover from. There is no undo. [1;38;5;196mType
carefully and look before you press Enter.[0m

[1;38;5;244mA safety habit[0m: list before you remove.
  [1;38;5;220mls[0m
  [1;38;5;220mrm <only-now-that-you-are-sure>[0m

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to take Stage 3's gate.[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 3 — GATE[0m

[1;38;5;244mRecall[0m (three questions, all three must be correct).
Then a [1;38;5;244mpractical task[0m.
[1;38;5;39mQ1: Which command creates an empty file?  (touch, mkdir, new, cat)[0m

[1;38;5;39mQ2: After [1;38;5;220mrm important.txt[0m, where is the file?  (~/.Trash, on disk, gone, depends)[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;39mQ3: What single command renames [38;5;109mold.txt[0m to [38;5;109mnew.txt[0m?[0m
  [1;38;5;220myour answer:[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 3 — GATE TASK[0m

You will work inside [38;5;109m/var/folders/jx/f_4n055973x5cwnyh_mhlw9h0000gn/T/shelltutor-sim-home-vlcywnbb/stage3[0m.

Do these, in order:

  1. create a file [38;5;109mnotes.txt[0m containing the word [1;38;5;244mhello[0m
     [2m(hint: [1;38;5;220mecho hello > notes.txt[0m[2m)[0m
  2. copy [38;5;109mnotes.txt[0m to [38;5;109mbackup.txt[0m
  3. rename [38;5;109mnotes.txt[0m to [38;5;109mdone.txt[0m
  4. remove [38;5;109mbackup.txt[0m

Then type [1;38;5;220mcheck[0m. The script will look at the folder.

[2mI will check: done.txt exists with 'hello' in it; notes.txt and[0m
[2mbackup.txt are gone.[0m

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mcheck[1;38;5;208m when done.[0m

[1;38;5;208mSTAGE 4 — Commands, streams, composition[0m

Three lessons, then a gate. You'll read a command's structure, check
whether a command exists, and chain commands together with pipes,
redirects, and globs.

Commands this stage:
  [1;38;5;220mcommand -v[0m   ask the shell if a program is installed
  [1;38;5;220mwc[0m           word, line, and character count
  [1;38;5;220mseq[0m           generate number sequences
  [1;38;5;220mhead[0m          first N lines of input
  [1;38;5;220msort[0m          sort lines
  [1;38;5;220mgrep[0m          select lines matching a pattern
  [1;38;5;220m|[0m             [1;38;5;244mpipe[0m: send one command's output into the next
  [1;38;5;220m>[0m             [1;38;5;244mredirect[0m: write output to a file (overwrites)
  [1;38;5;220m>>[0m            [1;38;5;244mappend[0m: add output to the end of a file
  [1;38;5;220m<[0m             [1;38;5;244minput redirect[0m: read a file into a command
  [1;38;5;220m*[0m

[1;38;5;244mglob[0m: match many filenames at once

[1;38;5;208m▶ Type [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m to begin lesson 4.1.[0m

[1;38;5;208m4.1 — reading a command[0m

A shell command has a small grammar:

  [1;38;5;244mcommand  options  arguments[0m

Examples:
  [1;38;5;220mls[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls -l[0m                    [2m# one option, no argument[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls -l /etc[0m               [2m# option + argument[0m
  [1;38;5;220mwc -l poem.txt[0m           [2m# count lines in a file[0m
  [1;38;5;220mecho "hello world"[0m       [2m# argument with a space — quoted[0m

[1;38;5;196mSpaces matter.[0m  The shell splits on spaces. If a filename
has a space, [1;38;5;244mquote it[0m or the shell will see two arguments:

  [1;38;5;220mvim "my notes.txt"[0m       [2m# opens one file[0m
  [1;38;5;220mvim my notes.txt[0m         [2m# opens TWO files: 'my' and 'notes.txt'[0m

[1;38;5;244mcommand -v[0m asks the shell whether a command exists.
  [1;38;5;220mcommand -v ls[0m            [2m# prints the path; exits 0[0m
  [1;38;5;220mcommand -v vim[0m           [2m# does Vim exist

on this system?[0m
  [1;38;5;220mcommand -v vimtutor[0m      [2m# does vimtutor?[0m

[1;38;5;208m▶ Try a few [1;38;5;220mcommand -v[1;38;5;208m probes, then [1;38;5;220mnext[1;38;5;208m.[0m

[1;38;5;208m4.2 — the pipe[0m

A [1;38;5;244mpipe[0m ( [1;38;5;220m|[0m ) sends the standard output of one
command into the standard input of the next. [1;38;5;196mMost important idea
in the shell.[0m

[1;38;5;220mwc[0m alone counts:
  [1;38;5;220mwc -l poem.txt[0m          [2m# lines in poem.txt[0m

[1;38;5;220mwc[0m via pipe counts [1;38;5;244mwhatever you piped in[0m:
  [1;38;5;220mseq 1 100 | wc -l[0m       [2m# 100[0m
  [1;38;5;220mls /usr/bin | wc -l[0m     [2m# how many programs are installed[0m
